flows.title: POST /api/orders – place order
flows.summary: Authenticates the caller, reserves stock, charges the card through the payment service and saves the order. Out-of-stock returns 409; other failures return 500.
flows.plain_summary: A customer places an order by sending POST /api/orders. First the auth middleware checks they are signed in; if not, the order stops with 401 Unauthorized. Otherwise ordersController.create hands the order to orderService.placeOrder, which asks inventoryRepo.reserve to set the items aside and then asks: All items available? If not, the customer gets 409 Out of stock. If yes, paymentClient.charge takes the money through the Payment service and orderRepo.save stores the order, so the customer receives 201 Created. If anything unexpected breaks on the way, the customer gets 500 Internal error.

nodes.label: POST /api/orders
nodes.description: Router mounted under /api in app.js. Runs the auth middleware, then the create controller.

nodes.label: auth middleware
nodes.description: Checks for an Authorization header and sets req.user. No token means the request stops with 401.

nodes.label: 401 Unauthorized
nodes.description: Request rejected before reaching the controller.

nodes.label: ordersController.create
nodes.description: Calls placeOrder with the user id and cart items, and maps errors to HTTP status codes.
nodes.snippet:
const order = await orderService.placeOrder(req.user.id, req.body.items);
res.status(201).json(order);

nodes.label: orderService.placeOrder
nodes.description: Core business logic: reserve stock, compute total, charge, then persist.

nodes.label: inventoryRepo.reserve
nodes.description: Runs one conditional UPDATE per item. Returns true only if every item was reserved.

nodes.label: All items available?
nodes.description: If any reservation failed, throws an OUT_OF_STOCK error.

nodes.label: 409 Out of stock
nodes.description: Controller catches err.code === 'OUT_OF_STOCK' and responds with 409.
nodes.note: Reserved stock for other items in the same order is not released. Possible inventory leak.

nodes.label: paymentClient.charge
nodes.description: POSTs to the payment service at PAYMENT_URL/charges. Throws if the response is not OK.

nodes.label: Payment service
nodes.description: Third-party HTTP API. The URL comes from the PAYMENT_URL env var.
nodes.note: Behaviour depends on environment configuration; not visible in this repo.

nodes.label: orderRepo.save
nodes.description: Inserts the order row and returns it.

nodes.label: 201 Created
nodes.description: Order JSON returned to the client.

nodes.label: 500 Internal error
nodes.description: Any other failure, e.g. a payment error, ends here.
nodes.note: If the charge succeeds but save fails, the customer is charged with no order stored.

notes: No database transaction wraps reserve → charge → save.
No retry or idempotency key on the payment call.

flows.title: POST /api/orders – sequence view
flows.summary: The same request as a sequence diagram (happy path plus the out-of-stock branch).
flows.plain_summary: The same order, shown as a conversation. The Client sends the request to OrdersController, which passes it to OrderService. OrderService asks InventoryRepo whether every item is in stock and, if so, asks PaymentClient to take the payment and then OrderRepo to save the order. If an item is out of stock the conversation ends early and the Client is told so.
